subject: Combining display and closed storage
hook: A sideboard that hides the hosting kit and gives you a serving top: here is how one gets made.
ig:
A sideboard that hides the hosting kit and gives you a serving top: here is how one gets made.

A good sideboard does two jobs. The cupboards swallow everything you need when people come round, and the top becomes a display surface most of the year and a serving station when it matters.

The process, from brief to finished piece:
1. The brief: what needs storing and how wide the top should be.
2. Cut on the sliding table panel saw and checked for square.
3. Edged with ABS, so the top and doors wipe clean.
4. Drilled for hinges, shelf pins and fixings on the boring machine.
5. Assembled in our Hanley workshop and quality-checked.
6. Finished, delivered and placed.

The last frame is the real thing, made in our workshop.

If you are planning ahead for hosting, our sideboards are linked in bio.
fb:
Planning to host this year? A sideboard is one of the hardest-working pieces you can have in a dining or living room.

The cupboards hide the spare glasses, napkins and serving dishes, and the top doubles as somewhere to set out drinks and nibbles when people arrive. Swipe through to see how one comes together in our Hanley workshop, from the brief to cutting, edging, drilling and assembly, finishing with an oak-effect sideboard we made.

alt: Six-frame sequence from a written brief to panels being cut, edged, drilled and assembled in a workshop, ending with a finished oak-effect sideboard.
on_asset: F1: The brief — Closed storage for glasses, napkins and serving dishes below, with a top wide enough to serve drinks from. | F2: Cut to size — Panels cut on the sliding table panel saw to the sizes on the drawing, checked for square. | F3: Edged — Every visible edge finished with ABS edging, so the top and doors wipe clean after a busy evening. | F4: Drilled — Hinge cups, shelf-pin rows and fixings drilled on the boring machine, so doors hang level and shelves can move. | F5: Assembled and checked — Built in our Hanley workshop, soft-close hinges fitted, then quality-checked before it leaves. | F6: Finished — An oak-effect sideboard with closed storage below and a clear top for display or serving.
